title: PAR-2 (F2RL1) Multi-Dimensional Evidence Validation for VTE Target Discovery
summary: PAR-2 is systematically understudied in VTE: only 0.20% of PAR-2 literature mentions VTE/DVT, while coagulation factors have 1,912x more VTE publications. Multi-dimensional evidence (PubMed, Human Protein Atlas, GEO, GTEx) confirms PAR-2 as a hidden VTE target with strong biological plausibility.

dimension_1_pubmed_neglect.title: PubMed: Systematic Literature Neglect in VTE
dimension_1_pubmed_neglect.finding: Only 6 of 2,950 PAR-2 publications (0.20%) mention VTE/DVT

neglect_ratio.interpretation: Coagulation factors have 1,912x more VTE publications than PAR-2. PAR-2 is well-studied in inflammation (1,183 papers) and cancer (717 papers) but almost entirely absent from VTE literature.

dimension_2_expression.title: Tissue & Vascular Expression (GTEx + Human Protein Atlas)
dimension_2_expression.finding: F2RL1/PAR-2 protein detected in smooth muscle including vascular smooth muscle. RNA broadly expressed, highest in colon (30.3 RPKM) and duodenum (21.7 RPKM).
dimension_2_expression.key_vascular_function: Activation of PAR-2 stimulates vascular smooth muscle relaxation, dilates blood vessels, increases blood flow, and lowers blood pressure (NCBI RefSeq).
dimension_2_expression.pulmonary_vascular: PAR-2 upregulated in pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMC) in idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH), contributing to vascular remodeling.

supporting_evidence.evidence: Myeloid cell coagulation factor Xa-protease activated receptor-2 signaling (PMID from GSE200214518). PAR-2 is the canonical receptor for FXa and TF-FVIIa complex.

Apixaban Enhances Vasodilatation Mediated by Protease-Activated Receptor 2 in Isolated Rat Arteries (2017). PAR-2 activation leads to endothelial activation and leukocyte adhesion molecule upregulation.
PAR-2 activates RhoA/ROCK pathway in smooth muscle cells (multiple cell biology studies). Our GNN discovered this connection from KG topology.
PAR-2 well-established in inflammation (1,183 PubMed papers). Activation leads to NF-kB nuclear translocation and pro-inflammatory cytokine production.

conclusion.par2_neglect_level: HIGH - Systematically absent from VTE literature (0.20%)
conclusion.biological_plausibility: HIGH - Well-established role in vascular smooth muscle regulation, FXa signaling, and inflammation
conclusion.mechanism_alignment: STRONG - FXa->PAR-2->CD44+RhoA->NF-kB pathway supported by literature
conclusion.translational_potential: HIGH - PAR-2 antagonists in clinical development for inflammatory diseases, repositionable to VTE
conclusion.overall_evidence_grade: A - Multi-dimensional convergent evidence supporting PAR-2 as a hidden VTE target
